title: How Do You Build A Chip That Helps AI Think? From Sand To Chip | TheOneApp, Explored EP11
desc:
In November 2026, the chip company Nvidia was in the news around the world. Why does everyone watch its chips? They are the engines of today's AI. Find out how a GPU is like a whole school hall of pupils, how a chip is made of tiny switches (P5 electric circuits), and then BE a grain of sand: melted into silicon, grown into a crystal, sliced into a wafer, and drawn on with light and shadow (P4 light) until you become a chip. Plus: Singapore makes about 1 in 10 of the world's chips, and why AI data centres need cooling (P4 heat).

Sources:
- Nvidia, Blackwell architecture (nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/technologies/blackwell-architecture): the Blackwell GPU has 208 billion transistors on two dies, so one die holds more than a hundred billion
- Nvidia's press release of 23 November 2026, filed with the US SEC (Form 8-K), and news reports of the same day (CBS News, NPR, CNBC): Jensen Huang reinstated as CEO, 11 days after stepping down on 12 November 2026
- Singapore Economic Development Board (edb.gov.sg/en/industries/semiconductor) and Singapore Department of Statistics (SingStat): Singapore makes about 1 in 10 of the world's chips
- Nvidia designs its chips in the United States (Santa Clara, California); TSMC makes the newest in Taiwan (news reports, 2025-2026)
- Wafers, crystals and clean rooms: reference articles on silicon wafers (300 mm wafers about 0.78 mm thick), the Czochralski method (crystals up to about 2 m long) and the ISO 14644 clean-room classes

title: One Teacher Or A Whole Hall? CPU vs GPU #Shorts
desc:
